    <h1>Jeroen<br>Monnee</h1>
    <p class="hero-role">Postdoctoral Researcher · University of Hamburg</p>
    <p class="hero-lead">
      I work at the interface of string theory, quantum gravity, and algebraic geometry.
      My research develops Hodge-theoretic and geometric methods to understand
      infinite-distance limits, emergent strings, flux compactifications, and quantum
      consistency conditions in Calabi–Yau compactifications.
    </p>

<section class="section-block">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div>
      <p class="section-kicker">Research programme</p>
      <h2>Geometry as a window into quantum gravity</h2>
    </div>
    <p class="section-intro">
      I study how the geometry of scalar-field spaces encodes the microscopic physics
      of string compactifications, with particular emphasis on asymptotic regimes where
      effective field theory is most strongly constrained.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="theme-grid">
    <article class="theme-card">
      <div class="theme-number">01</div>
      <h3>Emergent strings and infinite distance</h3>
      <p>
        Identifying the strings, towers of states, and higher-dimensional descriptions
        that emerge at boundaries of Calabi–Yau moduli spaces.
      </p>
    </article>

    <article class="theme-card">
      <div class="theme-number">02</div>
      <h3>Asymptotic Hodge theory</h3>
      <p>
        Turning structural theorems for degenerating Hodge structures into practical
        tools for periods, metrics, couplings, and flux potentials.
      </p>
    </article>

    <article class="theme-card">
      <div class="theme-number">03</div>
      <h3>Quantum consistency and finiteness</h3>
      <p>
        Testing when classical limits survive quantum corrections and how geometry
        constrains the landscape of effective theories and flux vacua.
      </p>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="section-block">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div>
      <p class="section-kicker">Selected work</p>
      <h2>Recent publications</h2>
    </div>
    <p class="section-intro">
      A selection of work on emergent strings, geometric degenerations, and quantum
      obstructions in four-dimensional string compactifications.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="work-grid">
    <article class="work-card">
      <div class="work-meta">Physical Review D · 2026</div>
      <h3>Quantum obstructions for \(\mathcal{N}=1\) infinite-distance limits</h3>
      <p>
        Quantum corrections can force a correlated scaling of different moduli sectors,
        obstructing limits that appear consistent in the classical effective action.
      </p>
      <div class="work-links">
        <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13470">arXiv</a>
        <a href="publications.html">Publication list</a>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article class="work-card">
      <div class="work-meta">Journal of High Energy Physics · 2026</div>
      <h3>Physics and geometry of complex-structure limits</h3>
      <p>
        A geometric interpretation of type II, III, and IV limits and the towers of
        BPS states that realise their emergent higher-dimensional physics.
      </p>
      <div class="work-links">
        <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP03(2026)063">Journal</a>
        <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07056">arXiv</a>
      </div>
    </article>

    <article class="work-card">
      <div class="work-meta">Journal of High Energy Physics · 2026</div>
      <h3>Emergent strings in Type IIB Calabi–Yau compactifications</h3>
      <p>
        A microscopic identification of emergent heterotic strings and accompanying
        towers of states in a broad class of type II limits.
      </p>
      <div class="work-links">
        <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP01(2026)140">Journal</a>
        <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01066">arXiv</a>
      </div>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>
